issues.problem: Misreading from the transliteration: the printed Devanagari is तमइव (tama iva = tamaḥ iva, regular visarga-dropping hiatus), not "tamaiva" with ai. The IAST "ai" collapses अ+इ. So the word is iva ("as it were"), not eva ("indeed"), exactly like the four other iva similes in this unit (kṣvelete iva, tudyete iva, pipīlikābhir iva, parikṛntann iva). The flag "tama eva" is therefore wrong and should be dropped; the draft also dropped "eva" from both translations.

summary: Independent review of p02/ch04 chunk 2 (units 41-80). Draft is sound overall: hedging, damaged-print handling (44, 54, 64, 65) and typo flags are plausible. Main finding: u48 'tamaiva' is the IAST of Devanagari तमइव = tama iva (simile iva, not eva), so the flag was wrong and 'as it were' was missing in both translations. Other errors: u43 Hindi reversed relation (nāḍī covered BY doṣas), u54 English case slip (instrumentals rendered with 'of'), u77 gram 'dvandva, m. nom. sg.' impossible for two disorders. Many minor items: modern names beside bilva, māṣa, vidārī, kuśa/kāśa, kāśmarya, parūṣaka; hedge madhuka consistently; hedge style in u71; Hindi पान/पेय; unflagged unclear word in u65 and a guess sitting in a gloss. Units needing a human decision: 41 (puṣpam arhati), 44/54/64/65 (damaged), 52/63 (āmagarbha), 59 (which mass is cooked with which rasa), 71 (go, attachment of bhūrisarpiṣkeṇa/ghṛtāḍhyena), 72 (bilva-śalāṭu one or two items), 77 (udāvarta-vibandha), 79 (scope of mūlānām; parivyādha, bhūtikā). Suggested join: 45+46 are one sentence (note added), 41-43 one flow.
glossary_suggestions: udūkhala is a variant of ulūkhala (mortar)
OCR confusions seen: ढ<->म (pramūḍha/pramuma), pta->ma (saptarātra/samarātra), dv->ddh (mārdvīka, vṛddhy-artham), st->sn (snāta), dh->d (saṃkṣudya), ṛ->i (vṛddhi/viddhi).

IAST 'ai' in the intake can be Devanagari अ+इ (tama iva), 'au' likewise: check the Devanagari before flagging a sandhi form (p02 ch04 u48). Sweep other chunks with a script comparing ai/au counts to ै/ौ counts.
bilva = 'bilva (bael)', māṣa = माष यानी उड़द, madhuka = 'probably licorice' (hedge in every unit), vidārī = probably Indian kudzu (Pueraria tuberosa); Hindi पान means betel leaf, use पेय for drinks.
A dvandva of two items cannot be 'm. nom. sg.' (dual -au or neuter samāhāra): check gram labels on dvandva compounds in nominative singular.
